title: Ischemic Maculopathy in Diabetic Retinopathy
summary: A devastating complication of diabetic retinopathy characterized by the loss of the foveal capillary network. Diagnosis relies on identifying foveal avascular zone (FAZ) enlargement and irregularity, often leading to irreversible central vision loss despite management of macular edema.

branches: Enlargement of the Foveal Avascular Zone (FAZ)
Disruption of the Perifoveal Capillary Arcade
Primary cause of 'Unexplained' vision loss in DR
Can coexist with Diabetic Macular Edema (DME)

sections.title: Pathophysiology Flow
content: 1. Chronic Hyperglycemia induces oxidative stress and AGES formation
2. Retinal capillary pericyte apoptosis and basement membrane thickening
3. Leukoembolization and capillary endothelial damage
4. Microvascular occlusion leading to capillary non-perfusion
5. Localized foveal hypoxia and FAZ expansion

sections.title: Ocular Examination Findings
content: VA: Poor vision (20/200 or worse) without significant DME
Amsler Grid: Central scotomas (often dense)
Fundoscopy: 'Featureless' macula (loss of normal luster)
Retinal Thinning: Appears as increased foveal depression reflex
Peripheral Signs: Often associated with NVD/NVE or extensive IRMA

sections.title: RED FLAGS: Warning Signs
content: Vision loss disproportionate to clinical macular edema
Rapid drop in VA following panretinal photocoagulation (PRP)
Failure of DME to respond to adequate anti-VEGF therapy
Ghost vessels in the macula on slit-lamp biomicroscopy
Extensive Cotton Wool Spots in the macular region

branches: FFA: Gold standard for perifoveal arcade integrity
OCTA: Visualizes SCP and DCP (Deep Capillary Plexus)
Microperimetry: Maps functional scotoma to ischemia
Adaptive Optics: Direct visualization of pericyte loss

sections.title: Management & Treatment Protocol
content: Step 1: Strict Systemic Control (HbA1c < 7.0%, BP < 130/80, Lipids)
Step 2: Anti-VEGF Therapy (May improve VA if DME is present, but won't reverse ischemia)
Step 3: Fenofibrate Therapy (ACCORD/FIELD studies show reduction in DR progression)
Step 4: Avoid Grid Laser Photocoagulation in areas of profound ischemia
Step 5: Visual Rehabilitation (Low vision aids for dense central scotomas)

sections.title: Surgical Considerations
content: PPV for TRD: Ischemia increases risk of post-op neovascular glaucoma
ILM Peeling: Controversial in ischemia; may worsen inner retinal mechanical stress
PRP: Ensure peripheral ischemia is treated to reduce VEGF load and protect the macula

branches: Initial VA (Best predictor of final outcome)

sections.title: Recent Advances & Trials
sections.content: Recent studies using OCT-Angiography (OCTA) have identified 'Dalla' or 'PAM' (Paracentral Acute Middle Maculopathy) as a potential biomarker for acute ischemic events in the inner nuclear layer. The PANORAMA study highlights the role of Aflibercept in reducing vision-threatening complications, though specific reversal of macular ischemia remains elusive. Research into Rho-kinase (ROCK) inhibitors and Tie2 activators (Faricimab) aims to stabilize the retinal vasculature more effectively than traditional VEGF monotherapy.

sections.title: Clinical Pearls for Residents
content: Always check FFA/OCTA if a patient has 20/200 vision but 'looks like' they only have mild NPDR.
Ischemic maculopathy is a contraindication to traditional macular grid laser in that quadrant.
The Deep Capillary Plexus (DCP) on OCTA is the primary oxygen source for the high-metabolic-demand synaptic layers; its loss correlates most strongly with poor VA.
Warn patients that despite 'clearing the fluid' with injections, vision may not improve if the FAZ is enlarged.
